cards.text: Ahab, king of Israel, just beat the army of Ben-hadad, king of Aram, but Ben-hadad got away on horseback (1 Kings 20:20-21). Now the prophet who promised Ahab that win comes back to him (1 Kings 20:13). And friend, he is NOT here to throw a victory party.

cards.question: The prophet tells Ahab to strengthen his position, because in the ___ the king of Aram will come up against him.

cards.text: Meanwhile, Ben-hadad's servants tell him why Israel won. They say, "Their gods are gods of the hills."

cards.question: So Ben-hadad's servants say the next fight with Israel should happen on the ___.

cards.text: That's losing at checkers and blaming the TABLE. And the plan keeps going: dismiss all the kings from their positions and replace them with other officers.

cards.question: What kind of army do Ben-hadad's servants tell him to raise?

answers.text: One just like the army he lost
One twice the size of the last
A smaller army that moves faster

cards.question: Ben-hadad turns down his servants' plan.

cards.text: Ben-hadad approves the plan and does it all, horse for horse and chariot for chariot. Then in the spring, right when the prophet said, he mobilizes the Arameans to fight Israel.

cards.question: Ben-hadad goes up to ___ to fight against Israel.

cards.text: Israel mobilizes too. They gather supplies and march out to meet the Arameans.

cards.question: The Israelites camp like two small flocks of goats. What does the Aramean army look like?

answers.text: It fits in one small valley

cards.text: That's me showing up to tug-of-war alone on my gold base, and the other side brought a whole TOWN. Then the man of God comes to Ahab with a word from the LORD: the Arameans have said the LORD is a god of the hills and not of the valleys.

cards.question: What does the LORD say He will do because of what the Arameans said about Him?

answers.text: Deliver their great army into Ahab's hand
Let the Arameans win on the plains
Send a storm to scatter both armies

cards.question: The LORD tells Ahab what this victory will show him. What is it?

cards.text: For seven days the two armies just camp across from each other. Seven DAYS of the world's longest staring contest.

cards.question: On the seventh day, Israel strikes down the Arameans.

cards.text: And it's not close. Israel strikes down a hundred thousand Aramean foot soldiers in one day.
The Arameans who are left flee into the city of Aphek. And then the wall falls on twenty-seven thousand of them.

cards.question: Ben-hadad flees into the city too, and he hides in an inner ___.

cards.text: Ben-hadad's servants come to him with a plan. They hope Ahab will spare Ben-hadad's life, because of something they've heard about the kings of the house of Israel.

cards.question: Ben-hadad's servants hope Ahab will spare Ben-hadad's life. What have they heard about the kings of the house of Israel?
Ben-hadad's servants plan to go out to Ahab dressed for battle.

cards.text: Their plan is sackcloth around their waists and ropes around their heads. So out they go to Ahab with a message: Ben-hadad says, "Please spare my life."
And Ahab answers, "Is he still alive? He is my brother." His BROTHER?! This is the man who demanded Ahab's silver, gold, wives and children (1 Kings 20:5).

cards.question: Ben-hadad's servants are looking for a sign of hope. When Ahab calls Ben-hadad his brother, what do they do?

answers.text: Quickly grab hold of that word
Ask Ahab to say it again

cards.text: They answer, "Yes, your brother Ben-hadad." And Ahab says, "Go and get him!"

cards.question: When Ben-hadad comes out, Ahab has him come up into his chariot.

cards.text: From hiding in an inner room to riding in Ahab's CHARIOT. Then Ben-hadad offers to restore the cities his father took from Ahab's father, and to let Ahab set up his own marketplaces in Damascus.

cards.question: Ben-hadad, king of Aram, offers Ahab cities and marketplaces. So what does Ahab do with him?

answers.text: Makes a treaty and sends him away
Keeps him as a prisoner in Samaria
Hands him over to the man of God

cards.text: Meanwhile, one of the sons of the prophets, a group of prophets, speaks by the word of the LORD. He says to his companion, "Strike me, please!"

cards.question: The prophet's companion does what the prophet asks.
The companion refuses to strike him. The request came by the word of the LORD, so what does the prophet say the companion has not done?

answers.text: Obeyed the voice of the LORD

cards.text: Then the prophet says that as soon as the man leaves him, a lion will kill him. And when he leaves, a lion finds him and kills him.
So the prophet finds another man and says that line again: "Strike me, please!"

cards.question: This time, the second man strikes the prophet.

cards.text: The blow wounds the prophet. Then he goes and waits on the road for the king, in disguise.

cards.question: The wounded prophet waits for the king, disguised with a ___ over his eyes.

cards.text: When Ahab passes by, the prophet cries out to him with a story from the middle of the battle. A man brought him a captive and said, "Guard this man!"
If the captive went missing for any reason, the prophet's life would be exchanged for the captive's life, or he would weigh out a talent of silver.
But while the prophet was busy here and there, the captive disappeared. That's me and my oven timer, friend: I set it down, get busy, and it's GONE.

cards.question: Ahab tells the prophet he can go free this time.

cards.text: Ahab says, "So shall your judgment be; you have pronounced it on yourself." Then the prophet quickly removes the bandage from his eyes.

cards.question: Once the bandage is off, Ahab recognizes him as one of the ___.
Now the prophet brings Ahab a word from the LORD. What does the LORD say Ahab let slip from his hand?

answers.text: The man God had devoted to destruction
The cities Aram took from his father
The silver his army won in battle

cards.question: The LORD says Ahab's life will be exchanged for Ben-hadad's life. What else does He say will be exchanged?
After that word from the LORD, how does the king of Israel go home to Samaria?

cards.text: And there we'll leave Ahab for now, friend. His story is far from done.
